citations.fact: Legacy angular/diffusivity radiance-to-flux weight WTDIFF initializes to 0.5; per-band SECDIFF may be overwritten later.
Surface radiance is fracs(1,g)*plankbnd(b). Per-gpoint rad stream is multiplied by WTDIFF; native band flux accumulation then multiplies by DELWAVE.
FLUXFAC is pi*2.e4 in legacy default-real kind; 1e4 is cm^-2 to m^-2 and the factor 2 combines with WTDIFF=0.5 in the standard stream convention.
plankbnd includes semiss; planklay/planklev are interpolated native Planck fields. planklev is the edge Planck function, not an independently g-point-resolved interface source.

legacy_derivation.per_layer_gpoint_source_radiance_W_m-2_s: fracs(l,g) * planklay(l,b) * DELWAVE(b) * WTDIFF * FLUXFAC / pi
legacy_derivation.equivalent_per_band_layer_source_radianc: sum_g_in_legacy_band[fracs(l,g) * planklay(l,b)] * DELWAVE(b) * WTDIFF * FLUXFAC / pi
legacy_derivation.surface_emitted_radiance_W_m-2_sr-1: sum_g_in_band[fracs(surface-adjacent-layer,g) * plankbnd(b)] * DELWAVE(b) * WTDIFF * FLUXFAC / pi; plankbnd already has semiss, so do not multiply by emissivity again
legacy_derivation.interface_rule: For a layer l, upward/downward interpolation terms use the SAME current-layer fraction fracs(l,g) times planklev at the corresponding top/bottom interface. At an interior interface the layer above and below therefore yield separate legacy face-source aggregates if their fracs differ; do not collapse them to one synthetic gpoint interface fraction.
legacy_derivation.native_band_flux_rule: RTE_BAND_*_NATIVE stores uflux/dflux after multiplication by WTDIFF but before DELWAVE and FLUXFAC. Reconstruct physical band flux as RTE_BAND_*_NATIVE * DELWAVE * FLUXFAC (no extra WTDIFF, no divide by pi). Sum bands in original order to check the packet’s W m^-2 output.

citations.fact: Source construction computes each gpoint source as interpolated per-band totplnk times the interpolated Planck fraction; layer source is emitted by gpoint.
At interior levels GP uses sqrt(pfrac(lower)*pfrac(upper)) times the level Planck function. At surface/top endpoints it uses the adjacent layer fraction.
The one-angle solver treats its transfer arrays as radiances and converts to flux with pi times quadrature weight.
The two-stream LW source routine documents source as W m^-2 sr^-1 and pi as the conversion to flux; this is consistent with the one-angle radiance conversion.
The band reducer sums GP gpoint fluxes in ascending recorded inclusive band limits; it does not average them.

gp_derivation.layer_band_source_radiance_W_m-2_sr-1: ordered sum of SOURCE_LAYER(column,layer,gpt) over the inclusive GP band limits
gp_derivation.level_band_source_radiance_W_m-2_sr-1: ordered sum of SOURCE_LEVEL(column,level,gpt) over inclusive GP limits; at interior levels this is the GP geometric-mean-fraction closure, not directly equivalent to a single legacy planklev field times one common fraction vector.
gp_derivation.surface_emitted_source: GP SOURCE_SURFACE is the raw Planck source (not already emissivity-weighted); multiply by the matching GP EMIS band-expanded-to-gpoint exactly once when comparing emitted boundary source to legacy plankbnd.
gp_derivation.units_caveat: The GP coefficient NetCDF totplnk has no explicit units attribute in this pinned file, while front-end/source comments call it integrated Planck irradiance and solver comments describe radiance W m^-2 sr^-1. Verify the pinned in-use source/solver conversion through same-engine reconstruction before interpreting cross-engine absolute source values as a strict unit-level oracle.

spectral_and_precision_rules.nonpaired_bands: Exclude bands 1-2 and 14-16 from paired conclusions; retain engine-native numbers only.
spectral_and_precision_rules.gpoint_policy: 140 legacy and 128 GP g-points are not pairable by index. Do not cross-interpolate or use unweighted gpoint averages.
spectral_and_precision_rules.precision: Legacy source and flux working arrays use default-real rb in this build. For a numerical comparator, preserve the engine’s operation order and source dtype; report absolute/relative deviations after conversion, not bitwise cross-engine equality.

safe_next_step: Pin packet/hash/execution receipt and verify its 55 legacy main fields match the historical packet; verify the actual-source hook is the terminal utility-v2 build and its source/dependency pins are unchanged.

Before comparing engines, confirm actual legacy PLAY/PLEV/TLAY/TLEV/TSFC/emissivity/N2 and dry geometry match the retained 45-layer matched-dry N2=0.7808 GP input. If not, stop or identify the state mismatch.

Validate legacy fractions normalize within each band/layer from the packet; reconstruct legacy flux from RTE_BAND_* using its saved order and scalars and confirm the packet’s ordinary legacy result. Reconstruct GP own outputs from GP saved recurrence/total tau before comparison.

For common bands 3-13 only, compare GP sum(SOURCE_LAYER) to fraction-weighted, converted legacy source radiance layer-by-layer. For levels, report the two adjacent-layer legacy face-weighted values separately alongside the GP geometric-mean level sum. Surface comparison applies emissivity once on each engine’s documented side.

Only after source-unit and same-engine reconstruction gates, compare common-band integrated fluxes. Keep optical-depth, Planck-source, angular/transport residuals separate; do not claim unique attribution if legacy tau or recurrence inputs are unavailable.
nonclaims: No numerical source-to-source differences were computed in this review.
No gpoint correspondence or exact source equivalence is claimed.
No accuracy, observational agreement, or physical-normal conclusion is supported by these unit identities alone.
The actual GP N2 sidecar is a solver diagnostic, not an independent radiative truth.
